ruling.recommended_action: Refund $5.89 excess distance fare to the rider's original payment method; send the driver the RD-7 notification-duty reminder and log the notification failure on his route compliance record (no formal warning — first such incident); record a driver violation for the reroute without traffic reason (RD-4 none). No account flag.
ruling.reasoning:
The trip ran 14.9 km against a 10.7 km optimal route, +4.2 km [F1], and the fare billed 4.18 km of excess distance at this trip's rate of $1.4098/km, i.e. $5.89 [F4]. The deviation is over 1 km, so RD-1 is met and the RD-2 matrix governs.

The single off-route segment is 21:43–21:50: 5.14 km driven against 1.44 km of optimal route (+3.70 km) via Jalan Bukit Merah, Kampong Bahru Road, Telok Blangah Road and Henderson Road [F3]. No traffic reason exists: the AYE was at speed band 7 (60–69 km/h) and the CTE at band 8 during the window, with no incident on record [F11][F12][F13], so RD-4 exempts nothing and a driver violation is recorded (RD-2/C3).

On consent, the rider's only pre-segment message, at 21:38, was "Any way also can, you decide, just bring me to NUS" [F7], accepted by the driver [F8]. That is a general route choice under RD-5 and it was sent before the segment began. The segment is a route driven to get to NUS — it starts with Jalan Bukit Merah and continues via Kampong Bahru Road, Telok Blangah Road and Henderson Road [F3] — not a loop that reaches nothing: the car kept moving toward the destination and dropped the rider at NUS, so the extra distance is the cost of the driver's chosen way rather than an errand or a lap returning to where it started. Because the agreement is a general route choice and this segment is the route actually chosen to reach NUS, it is exempt under RD-5, and there is no rider-named place for RD-3 to excuse (the rider named none, and the driver's post-trip naming of Telok Blangah/Henderson [F10] is his own claim, not consent).

The exemption leaves the trip at the optimal distance: nothing is left to refund. Under the RD-5 element there is no rider message, so the segment_counts path does not arise; the trace's no_action branch applies. Under TH-1/TH-2 (DISP-001, C1) an amount under $10 is decided by the system. Surge was 1.0×, so nothing is owed under SURGE [F5]; the rest of the $31.20 is base, time and platform fees [F6]. The driver has 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days [F16], so RD-6's flag condition is not met, and profiles do not decide the case [F15][F16].
